**Triage: `bug` · `security` · `priority:p1` · `domain:services` · `pm:blocked` on #14150 · `needs:contract-review` · type `Bug`.** Graded on arrival; ⛔ this is not an observation card.

## What I could re-verify, and what I could not

Re-run on `origin/main` @ `8094834` (the head after this card's `e854a531a`):

- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/package.json:29` → `"@better-auth/scim": "^1.7.2"` ✔
- `git grep -n "reconcileUser" -- 'packages/**/src/**'` → **0**, and the positive control `verifyBearerToken` over the identical path → **15**, so the instrument was answering ✔
- `auth-manager.ts:3255-3270` hands `scim()` exactly `connections: []` and `authentication.verifyBearerToken` — **no `identity` member**, read from the code, not inferred ✔
- `auth-manager.ts:3234` still reads "`active:false` → ban + session revoke (needs the admin plugin, forced on above)", and `:3236-3237` still says "the installed 1.7.1" against a `^1.7.2` pin ✔

⚠️ **One half I could NOT reproduce and am not echoing as confirmed:** `node_modules/@better-auth/scim` is not installed in this checkout, so `grep -ro "ban" node_modules/@better-auth/scim/dist` returns 0 here **vacuously** — nothing to grep is not the same reading as nothing found. The vendor-side table (0 occurrences at 1.7.0/1.7.1/1.7.2, 15 at 1.6.30, 17 at 1.7.0-rc.1) rests on the filer's measurement over installed and downloaded tarballs. It is a *checkable* claim and the repo-side half independently implies the same conclusion — a host callback that is never passed cannot write anything — so the finding stands either way. Whoever implements this re-runs the vendor grep with the package installed as step one.

## Why p1, and why this is not merely stale prose

Two consequences, and the second is the one that makes it p1:

1. **Deprovisioning is ineffective where it is not SSO-backed.** An IdP setting `active: false` revokes sessions and writes nothing. A user holding a local password signs straight back in. The card's own boundary is honest that an SSO-only user may be stopped by the IdP refusing them afterwards — but that is the IdP's mitigation, not this platform's, and `content/docs/references/system/auth-config.mdx` promises the author the platform's.
2. **A guard is green with an unreachable trigger.** `last-admin-guard.test.ts:552` drives `deprovision()` through a *simulated* `update: { banned: true }` rather than through `@better-auth/scim`. The ADR-0024 D5.2 last-administrator protection from #5892 therefore passes CI while the path it exists to intercept no longer writes `banned` at all. A gate that cannot fail is worse than an absent one, because it is counted.

## The fork, and only one limb is dispatchable

- **A — implement `identity.reconcileUser` and route it to this platform's own ban write** (`admin-ban-endpoints.ts` already owns that write *and* the last-admin guard). This restores declared = enforced: ADR-0071, the generated docs, and the #13816 construction-time refusal message all already assert this behaviour. Restoring a declared contract is the bug lane. **This is the limb that gets dispatched.**
- **B — accept session-revocation-only and restate the coupling everywhere.** ⛔ Not dispatchable by a seat. That retires a published capability and rewrites an operator-facing refusal message downward, which is the human floor twice over. If the implementer concludes A is infeasible against `1.7.2`, **stop and file a `needs-user-decision` card with the four facets** — ⛔ do not "resolve" the contradiction by editing the assertions to match the weaker behaviour. Prose that is false is a smaller problem than prose that has been quietly made true by lowering the promise.

⛔ Also do not touch the five stale assertion sites as a standalone cleanup. Under limb A they become true again untouched; editing them now buys a second edit and, worse, briefly makes the tree *look* consistent while the gap is open.

## Why `pm:blocked` on #14150

The shape of A depends on #14150's answer — whether the better-auth admin plugin can be mounted at action granularity (SCIM needing only `ban`), and whether a better-auth upgrade is in play. That card is `pm:dispatched` and held by the same session that filed this one, so the answer is close. ⚠️ Note for that seat: this finding partly **obsoletes #14150's own framing** — "SCIM 只要 ban" presumes a vendor SCIM path that reaches `ban`, and at `1.7.2` there is none; the reachable seam is the host callback. Worth folding into that measurement's write-up rather than discovering twice.

`needs:contract-review` because limb A changes sign-in accept/reject behaviour for a deactivated principal.

Size/model suggestion: M, at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. The pin that matters is an end-to-end one that drives `@better-auth/scim` itself — the existing simulated `deprovision()` helper is exactly the shape that let this rot unseen, so ⛔ do not extend it.

CONTRACT REVIEW — PR #14540 (#14360) at head 51000d482
Verdict: FAIL

① Derived judgments

  1. (a) Sign-in acceptance for a SCIM-deactivated principal. Before (merge-base 00ff228fe): `scim({...})` received only `connections` and `authentication.verifyBearerToken`; the vendor's identity facade ran `options.identity?.reconcileUser?.()` as a no-op and then `deleteUserSessions` (vendor `@better-auth/scim@1.7.2` `dist/index.mjs:4224-4225`), so `sys_user.banned` was never written and a local-password holder signed straight back in. After: the `identity.reconcileUser` member is passed (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts:3292-3294`) and routed to `reconcileScimUserLifecycle` (`auth-manager.ts:4933-4970`), which on `active: false` over an unbanned row calls `applyUserBan` with `SCIM_DEACTIVATION_BAN_REASON` and `banExpires: null` (`auth-manager.ts:4957-4964`, `admin-ban-endpoints.ts:140-151`). The vendor's admin plugin then refuses session creation with `FORBIDDEN` / `BANNED_USER` (better-auth `dist/plugins/admin/admin.mjs:33-47`). This is limb A of the triage ruling, and the reason string equals the one 1.6.30 wrote (`resolveSCIMActiveDeactivation`, 1.6.30 `dist/index.mjs:766`). RIGHT. Pinned by the suite at `scim-deactivation-reconcile-user.test.ts:383-406` (status 403 AND code at `:357-358`).

  2. (b) The un-ban rule. `active: true` lifts a ban only when `banReason === 'Deactivated via SCIM'` (`auth-manager.ts:4966-4969`); any other reason is left in place, and a deactivation over an already-banned row writes nothing (`auth-manager.ts:4958-4959`). Measured against the vendor the contract was declared on: 1.6.30 was IdP-authoritative — every PUT wrote `banned = (active === false)` and an `active: true` cleared `banReason`/`banExpires` unconditionally (1.6.30 `dist/index.mjs:1135`, `:769-770`), so the implemented rule is strictly tighter than the old contract, and relative to `main` it lifts only bans this same hook placed, so nothing an administrator wrote becomes IdP-reversible. The alternative (IdP lifts any ban) would let an attribute sync — every SCIM PUT carries `active: true` — re-admit a user banned for cause; that is a relaxation and is the maintainer's to grant, not the developer's. Judgment: RIGHT, a safe default that needs no ruling to land; the recorded open question is correctly left optional. Pinned at `test.ts:530-568` (attribute sync and explicit `active: true` both leave `Policy violation` in place; sign-in still `BANNED_USER` at `:542`, `:557`).

  3. (c) Last-administrator guard through SCIM. The guard is an engine `beforeUpdate` hook on `sys_user` at priority 20 (`last-admin-guard.ts:1561-1565`), fires when the payload turns `banned` on (`:1415-1429`; `isTrueFlag` accepts the `1` the adapter hands the engine, `:512-514`, `objectql-adapter.ts:816`), and refuses with `code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED'`, `status: 403` (`:523-533`, message `:1306-1315`). The SCIM write reaches it: `context.database.update` is the wrapped ObjectQL adapter (`objectql-adapter.ts:819-836`, core `dist/context/transaction.mjs:53-69`), whose `update` calls `dataEngine.update` with no caller context (`objectql-adapter.ts:958-979`), so the ADR-0092 guard bypasses (`identity-write-guard.ts:97-99`) and the break-glass guard judges it. The refusal is rethrown as `APIError('FORBIDDEN', { code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED' })` (`objectql-adapter.ts:606-615`, wrapper `:642-657` applied at `:838`), passed through unchanged by `runSCIMApplicationCallback` (vendor `index.mjs:1309-1319`), and rendered as the SCIM error envelope with `status: "403"` and `detail` = the guard's message (vendor `index.mjs:7166-7179`, `:1295-1303`). RIGHT: loud and correctly shaped. Production registers the same two guards in the same order at `kernel:ready` (`auth-plugin.ts:1262-1288`); the suite mirrors that (`test.ts:203-207`) and asserts envelope, status string and three detail fragments (`test.ts:460-466`), plus a positive control proving the guard is the refuser (`:486-502`).

  4. (d) The shared write. `applyUserBan` emits `banned: true, banReason, [banExpires], updatedAt` and `applyUserUnban` emits `banned: false, banReason: null, banExpires: null, updatedAt` (`admin-ban-endpoints.ts:140-161`) — field for field the vendor's own handlers (better-auth `dist/plugins/admin/routes.mjs:534-539`, `:474-479`). The `/admin/ban-user` mount keeps its exact prior ordering: userId → self-ban refusal → reason default → expiry validation → context → not-found → last-LOCAL-credential guard → write → `deleteUserSessions` (`admin-ban-endpoints.ts:198-239`); the diff replaced only the two inline `updateUser` calls. `...(banExpires ? { banExpires } : {})` at `:236` feeds `ban.banExpires !== undefined` at `:148`, so an absent expiry is omitted exactly as before. RIGHT. Session revocation stays outside the shared write (`:239`, vendor `index.mjs:4225`). RIGHT.

  5. (e) SCIM DELETE. On 1.7.2 `DELETE /Users/{id}` preserves a tombstone, deletes the `scimUser` source row and then calls `identity.reconcileUser` (vendor `index.mjs:6914-7012`, callback at `:7004`); with no active source the aggregate is inactive (`:4213-4218`), so the hook bans the account and the vendor revokes sessions. Before this PR that account kept its password and kept signing in. Stated in the PR body and the changeset; pinned at `test.ts:590-608`. RIGHT. Note the break-glass delete half no longer sees a `sys_user` delete on this path — the ban half covers it (not pinned for DELETE; see notes).

  6. (f) Idempotency. The hook reads the row first and writes only on a state transition (`auth-manager.ts:4938-4941`, `:4956-4969`); the vendor calls it on POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE (`index.mjs:6596`, `:6800`, `:6901`, `:7004`), including attribute-only PATCHes. RIGHT. Pinned at `test.ts:426-441` and `:511-527`.

  7. (a) again — WRONG, the accept set is not closed. A SCIM deactivation over a row that is banned with an expiry leaves the expiry in place: `if (banned) return;` (`auth-manager.ts:4958-4959`) does not look at `banExpires`.
